summary.text: From Lemnos to the Propontis the Argo's outward voyage was a chain of wonders and disasters — the Lemnian women, the accidental slaying of Cyzicus, the blind seer Phineus freed from the Harpies, the Symplegades clashing shut, and Amycus beaten in the boxing ring.

chapters.title: Lemnos and Hypsipyle
chapters.text: The first landfall was Lemnos, where the women had slain their husbands and Hypsipyle queen ruled alone. The Argonauts lay with the Lemnians and Jason took Hypsipyle to bed; twin sons were born, and Homer remembers Euneus who later sent wine from the isle to the Achaeans at Troy.

chapters.title: The death of Cyzicus
chapters.text: At the Propontis, Cyzicus king of the Doliones welcomed them with gifts and feasting. A storm drove the Argo back by night; mist and battle-cry confused the hosts, and Jason's men slew Cyzicus in the dark — only at dawn did they see the king they had killed was their host. His wife Clite hanged herself for grief.

chapters.title: Phineus and the Harpies
chapters.text: In Thrace the blind seer Phineus, tormented by the Harpies who snatched his food, begged the Argonauts for rescue. Zetes and Calais, the winged sons of Boreas, chased the monsters to the Strophades or drove them off for good — and Phineus, in gratitude, prophesied the road to Colchis and warned of the Clashing Rocks ahead.

chapters.title: The Symplegades
chapters.text: At the mouth of the Euxine Sea the Symplegades — the Clashing Rocks — crashed together whenever anything passed. Phineus counselled release a dove first; when it flew through with only its tail-feathers caught, the heroes rowed with all their might and Athena held back one rock so the Argo scraped through. After that the rocks stood fixed forever.

chapters.title: Amycus the Bebrycian
chapters.text: On the coast of Bithynia King Amycus forced all strangers to box with him and killed them. Polydeuces took the challenge, beat the king down, and the Bebrycians rushed on the Argonauts until Heracles and his comrades drove them off with spears.

chapters.title: Hylas lost
chapters.text: At Cios the boy Hylas, beloved of Heracles, went to fetch water and was pulled under by a nymph who loved his beauty. Heracles searched the hills in vain and would not sail on; the Argo left without him — Apollonius says the hero stayed behind, Apollodorus that he had already gone forward overland. The strongest Argonaut never reached Colchis.
